title: Extremal maximal-matchings conjecture for benzenoid chains
source: Tomislav Došlić and Taylor Short, “Maximal matchings in polyspiro and benzenoid chains”, arXiv:1511.00590 (2015); Appl. Anal. Discrete Math. 15 (2021) 179-200, Conjecture 5.19. (https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00590)

lanes.review: candidates-review-R4-opus-20261119-r1/REVIEW-331692.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS; required the graph-with-witness endpoint)
lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-331692-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-331692.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; BRIDGE sound and plainly stated; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: Among benzenoid chains with n hexagons, the helicene has the fewest maximal matchings. Lean proves: for every finite simple graph G carrying a hexagon-chain witness of length n (an ordered list of n six-cycles covering all vertices and edges, consecutive ones sharing exactly one edge, non-consecutive ones disjoint, the two shared edges of an interior hexagon disjoint), the number of inclusion-maximal matchings of the explicit helicene graph with n hexagons is at most that of G. The equivalence between the source's definition (a plane graph whose bounded faces are hexagons arranged in a chain) and the existence of such a witness, and the identification of the Lean helicene with the source's helicene, are proved in the paper in prose, because Mathlib has no plane embeddings. The minimizer is not unique at n = 4 (the zigzag chain ties at 288); for n = 5 to 10 the helicene and its mirror image are the only minimizers (referee's enumeration of 9,841 chains).
significance.caveat: The kernel-checked endpoint is stated for graphs with a hexagon-chain witness; the passage from the source's plane-graph definition to the witness (and back) is prose, not Lean, since Mathlib has no plane embeddings. An independent referee judged that bridge sound and complete. No uniqueness claim (the helicene ties with the zigzag chain at n = 4). Chen and Zhang (Filomat 2025) still list the problem as open.

root_basis: Root extracted the fourteen modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three, no forbidden tokens), and screened the Principia archive (300 ids), the omega registry and GitHub by id. An independent Opus referee checked the witness condition against the source definition in both directions, drew the Lean helicene and matched its counts to the source's values, enumerated 9,841 chains with independent code, read the paper line by line and supplied the revised paper used here. Root accepts the graph-with-witness endpoint with the prose bridge stated as a caveat.
